capitals.name: Gudme (Funen)
capitals.note: No capital is documented for an aggregate of Iron Age chieftaincies. Gudme is the one elite centre the opened pages place inside the first Cliopatria shape: 'The Gudme Hall complex, a ruling elite residence and cult site, was built in Denmark in the mid-3rd century'. Avaldsnes (c. 200) and Gamla Uppsala (3rd century on) are the page's other elite seats.

keyframe_review.note: Unverified: pages silent. 4,083 km2 (14 cells, 9.9-10.7E, 55.1-55.5N), the island group of Funen by my reading of the cells. The Roman Iron Age page dates its period '1-400 AD' and names no polity or ruler for 161-183; its nearest fact is the Gudme hall complex 'built in Denmark in the mid-3rd century', about seventy years after this shape begins. The Norse page is a disambiguation page and gives no area; no infobox area exists to compare.

Unverified: pages silent. 8,114 km2: Funen plus 24 cells at 10.7-11.7E, 60.0-60.9N (inland Norway north of the Oslofjord, my reading of the cells). No opened page names a polity there in 184-206. The Roman Iron Age page's one Norwegian fact, 'Norway's first royal seat was founded at Avaldsnes in c. 200 AD', is on the west coast, outside this shape; see norse_200.

New keyframe for 200-206. The Roman Iron Age page: 'Norway's first royal seat was founded at Avaldsnes in c. 200 AD'. Cliopatria's Norse shape (its western edge lies near 9-10E) does not reach Avaldsnes (about 5.3E, 59.4N), so the Norse shape is extended by a 25 km radius around the neighbouring town of Haugesund. The page gives the seat, not a boundary; the radius is the researcher's reading.

The Danes page says 'Around the middle of the first millennium, Jutland, Angeln, and southern Schleswig became part of Danish rule' and that 'Until around the 6th century, Jutland was the homeland of two other Germanic tribes' (Jutes in the north, Angles in the south), so the Jutland cells of this shape (45 of 156 Jutland cells) are plausible only as a late-5th-century reading. The same page puts the Danes in 'Zealand and Scania' and says their royal seat was on Zealand, and this shape holds none of either (0 of 29 Zealand cells, 0 of 98 Scania cells): they enter in the 500 shape. notes: Norse is a Cliopatria aggregate (Wikidata Q909583, 'Norse') for Iron Age Scandinavia, 161-499, not a documented state. None of the five pages opened (the page budget for 6 shapes) names a kingdom, ruler, capital or border in Scandinavia before 500; the Norse page itself is a disambiguation page. So the dossier keeps Cliopatria's shapes (unverified: pages silent), adds the one page-dated fact the pages give (Avaldsnes, 'Norway's first royal seat', c. 200) as a 25 km radius around Haugesund, and records every other event at confidence 1. type is state only because the schema has no better word for a Cliopatria aggregate; the map should draw it soft and lightly captioned. Shapes by my reading of their cells: 161 Funen; 184 plus inland Norway north of the Oslofjord; 207 plus eastern Jutland; 299 plus Gotland; 402/490 plus 285 cells across south-east Norway, southern Sweden and Jutland. The shape holds no Zealand and no Scania, which the Danes page names as the Danes' homeland ('the Danes were based in present-day Zealand and Scania'); both enter in the 500 shape of the Scandinavian minor kingdoms. Counterparts: every gain is from 'nobody' (the pages name no earlier holder); the Angles (slug angles, eu-06, 387-479) border the shape on Jutland's south from 402 and may deserve a contest or loss event if their dossier shows one. Wars: none, no opened page records a war of the period, so wars is empty (the Danes page's undated 'expelled the Heruli' belongs to the 6th century). Rulers: none documented. Gazetteer names needed (all real, used only in notes, not in regions): Gudme (Funen, 55.15N 10.68E) as the capital; Avaldsnes (Karmoy, about 59.35N 5.27E), replaced in regions by a 25 km radius around Haugesund; Funen as a region (Fyn is not an admin1 in the gazetteer). Pages not opened because the budget was spent: Germanic Iron Age, Proto-Norse language, Jordanes' Getica, Heruli, Jutes, Geats, Svear.
